description: Single-panel bright-field transmission electron micrograph of deformed Fe–30% Al. A 0.2 µm scale bar is drawn in the lower-right corner, and a black arrow springs from that corner pointing up-left, marking the imaging vector g = 1 1 0; the caption states the zone axis is near [0 0 1]. The field is dominated by long, near-straight dislocation lines running diagonally across the image, many appearing as closely spaced parallel pairs that form stepped or jogged configurations where they meet, consistent with dislocation reactions. Darker, denser dislocation tangles and clusters occupy the top edge of the field. Broad diagonal bands crossed by fine, closely spaced fringes traverse much of the area. No numeric values are printed beyond the scale bar, and no crystallographic indices or diffraction pattern appear in the frame. Per the caption and citing text: the straight segments are screw-oriented superdislocations, the paired lines are dislocation pairs produced by dislocation reactions rather than the 2(1/2)⟨111⟩ partials of glissile superdislocations, and the fringes are residual APBII contrast from the weakly DO3-ordered material deformed by superdislocation motion.

observations.observation: The figure is one bright-field TEM micrograph carrying a 0.2 µm scale bar in the lower-right corner.
A black arrow originating at the lower right points up-left, marking the imaging vector g = 1 1 0 as stated in the caption; the vector itself is not labelled with text in the pixels.
Long, near-straight dislocation segments run diagonally across the field, several of them paired as closely spaced parallel traces.
Dislocation traces step or jog where they intersect, producing stepped configurations rather than smooth continuous lines.
Dense dark dislocation tangles and clusters are concentrated along the top edge of the micrograph.
Broad diagonal bands crossed by fine, closely spaced fringes traverse much of the field.
The specimen is deformed Fe–30% Al and the zone axis is near [0 0 1], per the caption.
The citing text states that superdislocations are often rather straight in screw orientations and that reactions between dislocations lead to the stepped structures seen here.
The citing text states that the dislocation pairs are the result of dislocation reactions and do not correspond to the partials of the glissile superdislocations.

The citing text states that the fringes traversing the area are due to residual contrast of APBII fringes produced during deformation of this weakly DO3 ordered material, the pairs of (1/2)1 1 1 partials destroying the order during movement.

The citing text states deformation occurs by movement of superdislocations composed of 2 (1/2) 1 1 1 partial dislocations, with small separation of the partials because the APBI fault energy is high in Fe–30% Al.
